title: Product Sans / ‘a’ Swap
slide_intent: Use a controlled alternate when repeated forms blur the distinction between a parent logo and a product name.
strategic_value: A double-story a can let Google’s product names retain their own character beside the circular logo.
demonstration: Two large a forms at left align with two Maps specimens at right, comparing a schoolbook form with a double-story alternate.
practical_value: Compare alternate glyphs inside the actual product name before selecting one only for its isolated appearance.

reference_purposes.Intent: The caption explains that alternates avoid redundancy in product lockups and give the product name its own character.
reference_purposes.Expression: The paired a and Maps specimens show the difference clearly.
reference_purposes.Application: The isolated glyph comparison is tested within the product name Maps.

ingredient.name: Double-story a alternate
ingredient.role: Distinguish product-name texture from the circular Google logo.
ingredient.application: Compare the double-story alternate with the schoolbook form in a product lockup, as the Maps example demonstrates.
ingredient.scope: The 2015 specimen’s product-lockup example; not a requirement to replace every a in all typography.
